Geometrical identification of dof relation for 3D elements
body:
This PR fixes #285 . For 1D and 2D elements, the DofHandler still uses a topological identification (I haven't found any bug yet). For **3D elements**, the identification stays **topological for degree <= 2**, but switches to **geometrical for degree >= 3**.

Just in case, I've introduced a `geom_factor` in the constructor of `SingleFESpace` to eventually play with the tolerance.

Also, periodicity for continuous FESpaces has been introduced using the API: `TrialFESpace(fs, mesh; periodicity = <list of BoundaryFaceDomain>)`

title: Looking for bugs with an LLM
body:
## Code Review Report: Bcube.jl - Potential Mistakes and Errors

After reviewing the source code of the Bcube.jl package, I found the following potential issues:

> [!WARNING]
> Items 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 13 have already been fixed.

---

### 1. **BUG: `Base.eltype` uses wrong syntax** (`src/mesh/mesh.jl`, line 73)
```julia
Base.eltype(::MeshConnectivity{C}) where {C <: AbstractConnectivity} = eltype{C}
```
`eltype{C}` uses curly braces (type parameterisation syntax) instead of parentheses for a function call. This should be `eltype(C)`.
---

### 2. **BUG: `Base.iterate` ignores state, causing infinite loop** (`src/mesh/mesh.jl`, lines 74-76)
```julia
function Base.iterate(c::MeshConnectivity{C}, i = 1) where {C <: AbstractConnectivity}
    return iterate(indices(c); i = 1)
end
```
The state parameter `i` is never forwarded — it always resets to `1`, which would cause an infinite loop if `indices(c)` has more than one element. Also, the keyword argument syntax `; i = 1` is wrong for `Base.iterate`. Should be:
```julia
return iterate(indices(c), i)
```

---

### 3. **BUG: `edges()` accessor uses wrong symbol** (`src/mesh/mesh.jl`, line 302)
```julia
edges(mesh::Mesh) = entities(mesh, :edges)
```
Uses `:edges` (plural) instead of `:edge` (singular). All other accessors use the singular form (`:node`, `:face`, `:cell`). This will throw a `KeyError` when called as it won't find the `:edges` key.

---

### 4. **BUG: `CellDomain` has undefined type parameter `I`** (`src/mesh/domain.jl`, line 163)
```julia
struct CellDomain{M, SD, T} <: AbstractCellDomain{M, I}
```
`I` is not declared as a type parameter of `CellDomain`, so it refers to an undefined identifier. Either `I` should be added to the type parameters, or removed from the supertype:
```julia
struct CellDomain{M, SD, T} <: AbstractCellDomain{M}
```
(assuming `AbstractCellDomain` is adjusted), or `I` should be made a proper type parameter.

---

### 5. **BUG: `change_domain` error message references undefined variable `f`** (`src/cellfunction/eval_point.jl`, line 38)
```julia
function change_domain(a, input_domain::DomainStyle, target_domain::DomainStyle)
    error("`change_domain` is not defined for $(typeof(f))")
end
```
`f` is not defined in this scope. Should be `typeof(a)`.

---

### 6. **BUG: `_two_cubes_mesh` has incorrect z-coordinates** (`src/mesh/mesh_generator.jl`, lines 857-861)
```julia
Node(SA[1.0, 0.0, zmin]),  # node 8 — should be zmax
Node(SA[2.0, 0.0, zmin]),  # node 9 — should be zmax
Node(SA[1.0, 0.1, zmin]),  # node 11 — should be zmax
Node(SA[2.0, 0.1, zmin]),  # node 12 — should be zmax
```
According to the ASCII diagram, nodes 7-12 should be at `z=zmax`, but only nodes 7 and 10 use `zmax`. Nodes 8, 9, 11, 12 incorrectly use `zmin`, making the two "cubes" degenerate.

---

### 7. **BUG: `_cube_pile_mesh` has duplicate node and invalid connectivity** (`src/mesh/mesh_generator.jl`)
- **Lines 918-919**: Nodes 18 and 19 have identical coordinates `(2.0, 1.0, 3.0)`
  ```julia
  Node(SA[2.0, 1.0, 3.0]),  # node 18
  Node(SA[2.0, 1.0, 3.0]),  # node 19 — duplicate!
  ```
- **Line 933**: `cube4 = [10, 11, 14, 13, 17, 18, 20, 19]` references node 20, but only 19 nodes are defined. This will throw a `BoundsError`.

---

### 8. **BUG: Duplicate assertion** (`src/mesh/mesh.jl`, lines 451-452)
```julia
@assert (mesh.bc_names ≠ nothing && mesh.bc_nodes ≠ nothing) "bc_names and bc_nodes must be defined"
@assert (mesh.bc_names ≠ nothing && mesh.bc_nodes ≠ nothing) "bc_names and bc_nodes must be defined"
```
The same assertion is written twice consecutively. One should be removed.

---

### 9. **Code smell: Dead code in `_build_boundary_faces!`** (`src/mesh/mesh.jl`, lines 432-433)
```julia
bc_faces = Dict{Int, Vector{Int}}()
bc_faces = (; zip(keys(bc_nodes), [...])...)
```
A `Dict` is created and immediately overwritten with a `NamedTuple`. The `Dict` allocation is unnecessary dead code.

---

### 10. **Typo in error message** (`src/function_space/function_space.jl`, line 322)
```julia
error("'get_quadrature' is not invalid for modal basis functions")
```
Double negative: "is not invalid" should be "is not valid" or "is invalid".

---

### 11. **Comment mismatch** (`src/mesh/mesh_generator.jl`, line 821)
```julia
# Number of nodes of each cell : always 2
cell2nnodes = 3 * ones(Int, n)
```
Comment says "always 2" but sets cells to have 3 nodes (quadratic elements).

---

### 12. **Inconsistent keyword assertion message** (`src/quadrature/quadrature.jl`, line 24)
```julia
@assert D isa Integer && D ≥ 0 "'D' must be a positive Integer"
```
The assertion allows `D ≥ 0` (zero is non-negative, not positive), but the message says "positive". Should say "non-negative Integer".

---

### 13. **`mapping_jacobian_inv` for `Bar2_t` has inconsistent broadcasting** (`src/mapping/mapping.jl`, lines 369-371)
```julia
function mapping_jacobian_inv(::Bar2_t, cnodes, ξ)
    @SMatrix[2.0 / (cnodes[2].x[1] .- cnodes[1].x[1])]
end
```
Uses `.-` (elementwise subtraction) inside a scalar division. If `cnodes[2].x[1]` is a scalar (which it should be for a 1D Bar2), the `.` is unnecessary. If it's a vector, the result type is inconsistent with the `@SMatrix` annotation.

---

These issues range from critical bugs (items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7) that would cause runtime errors or incorrect behavior, to minor inconsistencies (items 8-13). The most critical are the `Base.iterate` infinite loop bug (#2), the `eltype` syntax error (#1), the `edges` symbol mismatch (#3), and the degenerate/invalid test meshes (#6, #7).

title: dcontract in MultiFESpace bilinear assembly
body:
The following MWE errors with Bcube v0.4.2:
```julia
module tmp
using Bcube
using LinearAlgebra

function run()
    mesh = one_cell_mesh(:quad)
    dΩ = Measure(CellDomain(mesh), 1)

    U_vec = TrialFESpace(FunctionSpace(:Lagrange, 1), mesh; size = 2)
    V_vec = TestFESpace(U_vec)
    U_sca = TrialFESpace(FunctionSpace(:Lagrange, 1), mesh)
    V_sca = TestFESpace(U_sca)
    U = MultiFESpace(U_vec, U_sca)
    V = MultiFESpace(V_vec, V_sca)

    function f(q, ∇q, φ, ∇φ)
        u, p = q
        ∇u, ∇p = ∇q
        φ_u, φ_p = φ
        ∇φ_u, ∇φ_p = ∇φ
        return ∇u ⊡ ∇φ_u
    end

    a(q, φ) = ∫(f∘(q, map(∇, q), φ, map(∇, φ)))dΩ
    assemble_bilinear(a, U, V) # ERROR
end

run()

end
```
with
```julia
ERROR: LoadError: MethodError: dcontract(::Bcube.LazyOperators.MapOver{NTuple{8, Bcube.LazyOperators.MapOver{NTuple{…}}}}, ::Bcube.LazyOperators.NullOperator) is ambiguous.

Candidates:
  dcontract(a::Bcube.LazyOperators.MapOver, b)
    @ Bcube .julia\packages\Bcube\ObDWH\src\algebra\algebra.jl:152
  dcontract(a, ::Bcube.LazyOperators.NullOperator)
    @ Bcube .julia\packages\Bcube\ObDWH\src\algebra\algebra.jl:162

Possible fix, define
  dcontract(::Bcube.LazyOperators.MapOver, ::Bcube.LazyOperators.NullOperator)
```

title: `BoundaryFaceDomain` for a mesh without boundaries
body:
We have introduced a new "bug" when changing the `BoundaryFaceDomain` constructors. See the MWE:
```julia
mesh = circle_mesh(5)
b = BoundaryFaceDomain(mesh) # StackOverFlow
```

We could argue that this is not a "bug" because building the `BoundaryFaceDomain` for a mesh without boundaries has no sense. But we should either:
1. throw a clear error to the user : we just have to define `BoundaryFaceDomain(mesh, ::Tuple{}) = error("Cannot build a BoundaryFaceDomain because no boundary face was found.")`
2. build a `BoundaryFaceDomain` without any face in it (seems a bit more complicated, but should be possible)

The problem with solution 1. is here : https://github.com/bcube-project/Bcube.jl/blob/7162ca369371fd75513e260aa5fecc1c59c1afe9/src/feoperator/limiter.jl#L160, ie a call to the limiter triggers the construction of a `BoundaryFaceDomain`, so we would have to insert an `if nfaces > 0` here.

In the end:
* either we throw an error for `BoundaryFaceDomain` of a mesh without boundaries AND insert an `if` in the limiter
* either we build an "empty" `BoundaryFaceDomain` and we don't touch the limiter

In the meantime, the `transport_hypersurface` example from `BcubeTutorials` is broken...

title: Could we avoid `get_fe_functions`?
body:
A lot of `Bcube`-beginners (and even myself) often fall in the following "trap", ie the need for a `get_fe_functions` in the form definitions when using a `MultiFESpace`:
```julia
module tmp
using Bcube
using LinearAlgebra

function run()
    mesh = one_cell_mesh(:line)
    dΩ = Measure(CellDomain(mesh), 1)
    fs = FunctionSpace(:Lagrange, 0)

    U1 = TrialFESpace(fs, mesh)
    V1 = TestFESpace(U1)
    u1 = FEFunction(U1)
    f1(u, v) = u ⋅ v
    l1(v1) = ∫(f1 ∘ (u1, v1))dΩ
    assemble_linear(l1, V1)

    U = MultiFESpace(U1, U1)
    V = MultiFESpace(V1, V1)
    u = FEFunction(U)
    function f2(u, v)
        u1, u2 = u
        v1, v2 = v
        return u1 ⋅ v1 + u2 ⋅ v2
    end
    l(v) = ∫(f2 ∘ (get_fe_functions(u), v))dΩ # Note the mandatory `get_fe_functions`
    assemble_linear(l, V)
end

run()
end
```

How could we improve this? Ideally, it should "work" even without the `get_fe_functions`....

title: Implement `convert_to_lagrange_P1` for `MeshPointData`
body:
```julia
"""
    lagrange_P1_node_to_idof(mesh)

WARNING : I'm facing situations where there are mesh nodes not belonging to any element.
So the "node2idof" and "idof2node" are not strictly a permutation.
"""
function lagrange_P1_node_to_idof(mesh)
    fs = FunctionSpace(:Lagrange, 1)
    U = TrialFESpace(fs, mesh)
    dhl = Bcube._get_dhl(U)
    node2idof = zeros(Int, nnodes(mesh))
    idof2node = zeros(Int, get_ndofs(U))
    for cellInfo in Bcube.DomainIterator(CellDomain(mesh))
        shape = Bcube.shape(Bcube.celltype(cellInfo))
        icell = Bcube.cellindex(cellInfo)
        c2n = Bcube.get_nodes_index(cellInfo)
        for (ivertex_l, idofs_l) in enumerate(Bcube.idof_by_vertex(fs, shape))
            ivertex_g = c2n[ivertex_l]
            idof_g = Bcube.get_dof(dhl, icell, 1, idofs_l[1]) # there is only one dof per vertex with Lagrange P1
            node2idof[ivertex_g] = idof_g
            idof2node[idof_g] = ivertex_g
        end
    end
    return node2idof, idof2node
end
```

title: Introducing subdomains

`Domain` is now composed of a tuple of `SubDomain` whose element indices correspond to a unique type of element. It allows type-stable loop over a domain with the new functions `foreach_element` and `map_element`.

body: Intended to avoid stackoverflow for computations with elements with large number of dofs (for instance vector-FESpace of degree 2 in 3D).

body: Avoid forming SMatrix in bilinear assemble to enable high order 3D elements. For this 1st version I let the old code commented below all my modifs

title: Allocations in `get_coords`
body: The current implementation of `get_coords` for Lagrange triangles (https://github.com/bcube-project/Bcube.jl/blob/5862538ffbd1829c677d67abedb231d1d0da429a/src/function_space/lagrange.jl#L844) is allocating. We can get rid of the allocations.

title: Implement `idof_by_volume`
body:
We have `idof_by_edge`, we have `idof_by_face`, but we're missing an `idof_by_volume` return dofs lying "inside" the element (ie not a vertex, not on a edge, not on a face).

The implementation could be performed with a _@generated_ by considering all the dofs and removing the ones from `idof_by_face_with_bounds`.

title: Prism as cartesian product between Triangle and Line
body: I've modified the `Prism` implementation (shape functions, dofs and quadrature) in order simplify & allow for higher Lagrange elements.

title: `update_b!` ambiguity
body:
The following code
```julia
using Bcube

mesh = one_cell_mesh(:line)

fs = FunctionSpace(:Lagrange, 1)
U_p = TrialFESpace(fs, mesh)
U_u = TrialFESpace(fs, mesh)

V_p = TestFESpace(U_p)
V_u = TestFESpace(U_u)

V = MultiFESpace(V_p, V_u)

dΩ = Measure(CellDomain(mesh), 1)
l((v_u, v_p)) = ∫(v_p)dΩ

assemble_linear(l, V)
```

produces the following error

```julia
ERROR: LoadError: MethodError: __update_b!(::SubArray{…}, ::SubArray{…}, ::Bcube.LazyOperators.NullOperator, ::Bcube.BcubeBackendCPUSerial) is ambiguous.

Candidates:
  __update_b!(b::AbstractVector, dofs, vals::Bcube.LazyOperators.NullOperator, backend::Bcube.AbstractBcubeBackend)       
    @ Bcube Bcube\s2j9E\src\assembler\assembler.jl:522
  __update_b!(b::AbstractVector, dofs, vals, backend::Bcube.BcubeBackendCPUSerial)
    @ Bcube Bcube\s2j9E\src\assembler\assembler.jl:515

Possible fix, define
  __update_b!(::AbstractVector, ::Any, ::Bcube.LazyOperators.NullOperator, ::Bcube.BcubeBackendCPUSerial)
```
